samples.blindSolveReason: For either displayed positive integer b, put a_b=1 and every other coefficient zero. This is elementary existence, so sample0 is below the requested advanced level.

Use k=sN and Stirling in the positive Poisson moment sum. Maximize log(s)+s log(lambda/s)+s-lambda; its stationary equation is s log(s/lambda)=1, solved by s=2. Tail domination completes the Laplace principle.
The exact Pade remainder is (-1)^N z^(2N+1)/(N!)^2 times integral exp(zt)t^N(1-t)^N. At z=N/2, Stirling supplies e squared/4 and the integral root is its positive maximum at t=(sqrt17-3)/2.
Schur weights j^(-1/2),k^(-1/2) reduce both row and column sums to the integral pi/sqrt2. Truncated reciprocal-square-root sequences on a long logarithmic range approach that constant.

For weights k choose c_k=((k+1)/2)*((k+2)/(k+1))^((k+1)/2). Weighted AM-GM telescopes the product and the sum of4/[n(n+1)(n+2)], leaving c_k/((k+1)/2)<sqrt(e). Truncated a_k=1/k makes the quotient tend to sqrt(e).
The unequal Dixon constant-term identity gives(6N)!/[N!(2N)!(3N)!]. Stirling cancels the exponential432^N and leaves1/(2pi N).
Fixed-row telescoping gives-b/((m+b)(m+b+1)); fixed-column telescoping gives a/((n+a)(n+a+1)). The square sum is the antisymmetric equal-start square minus a finite strip, yielding(a-b)/(2(a+b)).
Discrete Hardy has sharp constant(p/(p-1))^p. Its standard summation-by-parts/Hölder upper bound and truncated critical power a_n=n^(-1/p) give the same constant at p=3/2.
Differentiate the product with roots cos(2pi k/13): the sum is T_13 prime(3/2)/(T_13(3/2)-1). Chebyshev recurrence gives the exact rational value.
